source.title: Spectral Unforgetting: Post-Hoc Recovery of Damaged Capabilities Without Retraining

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign supervised fine-tuning changes harmful-request safety behavior, using different models, tasks, and evaluation measures from the original fine-tuning study.
record.gate_note: The safety evaluation reports Base, FT, and DG-Hard values for HarmBench refusal, XSTest over-refusal, and StrongREJECT harmfulness. HarmBench and StrongREJECT bear on harmful compliance; XSTest measures over-refusal on safe prompts and is not recorded as a result for these claim versions. The spectral plots and capability-repair results do not measure per-token KL, opening-token bypasses, or safety localization in weights.
record.test_reason: Section 4.7 and Table 4 compare Base and benign full-SFT checkpoints of two safety-aligned Instruct models on HarmBench refusal and StrongREJECT harmfulness. This bears directly on V2 (benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance), using different tasks, models and benchmarks from the original study. The rest of the paper is capability-repair work (DG-Hard) and does not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that benign SFT can incidentally erode safety and that DG-Hard recovers most of the gap on the Llama cells without alignment data. They also acknowledge that FT improved some safety axes on Qwen cells, and they frame the safety recovery as following from the same spectral-residual mechanism, not as a designed objective.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign full-parameter SFT on task datasets, with three epochs and a single seed per cell, rather than harmful-example fine-tuning or a few-example intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety outcomes differ by model, fine-tuning task, and metric; Qwen WikiQA shifts HarmBench refusal and XSTest over-refusal in opposite directions.

fits_no_version.finding: DG-Hard spectral thresholding of the fine-tuning delta moves HarmBench and StrongREJECT values back toward Base after benign SFT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Checkpoint-only spectral denoising of the fine-tuning delta partly restores safety eroded by benign fine-tuning, without alignment data.

fits_no_version.finding: Qwen WikiQA SFT raised XSTest over-refusal from 2.8 to 15.6 while also raising harmful-prompt refusal. This is safety drift toward over-refusal, not toward harmful compliance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning can shift refusal behaviour in either direction, including toward over-refusal of safe prompts.

record.problems: Safety outcomes are reported for only three of the seven fine-tuning tasks per model; the study states a single seed per cell and reports no uncertainty estimates for Table 4 safety values. Only two model families are evaluated.

untested.parts: Few-example benign fine-tuning (e.g., 10-100 examples), identity-shifting or deliberately chosen benign data, larger models, multiple seeds. Safety is reported for only 3 of 7 tasks per model, and only two small models are tested.
Not tested: no per-token KL by response position.
Not tested: no prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Not tested for safety. The spectral and layer-class analyses concern capability noise, not where safety is localized.
Not tested. DG-Hard is a post-hoc repair, not training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens.

missing.what: XSTest over-refusal Base/FT values for all six cells (e.g., Qwen WikiQA 2.8→15.6). These are not V2 compliance results but show the direction of safety drift.

record.verdict_notes: Safety is a side experiment in a capability-repair paper. Each cell has a single seed, there are no uncertainty estimates in Table 4, and the stated drift floor is about ±1 pp on HarmBench (n=200). The Base values for the same base model vary across task rows (HarmBench 95-97 on Qwen, 87.5-88 on Llama; StrongREJECT 0.0076 vs 0.0160 on Qwen), which suggests evaluation drift or table misalignment. Small deltas should therefore be read cautiously. The original-source paper (Qi et al.) is cited but is not this study.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or few-to-few-hundred-example harmful datasets.
Tests benign full-parameter SFT across selected tasks, not few-example fine-tuning or a broad range of benign-data compositions; safety is reported for three of seven tasks per model.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement across response positions.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding interventions aimed at bypassing refusal.
The paper does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The proposed signal-plus-noise account concerns fine-tuning deltas generally; the study does not test why safety behavior would be shallow.
No training that spreads safety beyond initial response tokens or evaluation of whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.reason: HarmBench refusal fell 12.5, 8.5 and 15 pp, and StrongREJECT harm rose 0.048→0.140 and 0.054→0.080 (r1, r4, r6, r10, r12).
relationships.display_finding: HarmBench refusal fell by 12.5, 8.5 and 15 percentage points, and StrongREJECT harm rose from 0.048 to 0.140 and from 0.054 to 0.080.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct after Winogrande and MedQA SFT (both metrics); Qwen3.5-4B after Winogrande SFT (HarmBench)
source_check.reason: Refusal decreases in r1, r4 and r6; harmfulness increases in r10 and r12. These results follow V2 in the named settings.

relationships.condition: Llama WikiQA SFT; Qwen Winogrande and MedQA on StrongREJECT
relationships.reason: Effects were marginal or nil: a 3 pp refusal drop and negligible or zero StrongREJECT changes. For Qwen Winogrande, the refusal drop is not matched by any StrongREJECT change, so the result depends on the metric (r5, r7, r9, r11).
relationships.display_finding: Effects were marginal or nil, with a 3 pp refusal drop and negligible or zero StrongREJECT changes. For Qwen on Winogrande, the refusal drop had no matching StrongREJECT change, so the result depended on the metric.

relationships.display_finding: Refusal rose to 100% and 99.5% and StrongREJECT harm fell from 0.016 to 0.008; the authors say fine-tuning incidentally improved a safety axis.
